data.name: AlreadyRunningMessage
data.value: FiveM Diagnostics is already running, but the running window did not respond. Look for the icon in the notification area.

data.name: QuickStartIntro
data.value: Just play: the session follows FiveM, and the app marks bad frames on its own.

data.name: QuickStartStepOne
data.value: 1. Start FiveM, or press Start session.

data.name: QuickStartStepTwo
data.value: 2. Press the hotkey when it stutters.

data.name: QuickStartStepThree
data.value: 3. Afterwards, open Share and create a zip of the evening for whoever is helping you.

data.name: QuickStartDeepNote
data.value: Marking stutter also saves a short deep capture of the seconds before, which needs administrator rights.

data.name: PresentMonStatusConfigured
data.value: PresentMon is configured. Frame telemetry will be included.

data.name: PresentMonStatusAutoDetected
data.value: PresentMon was found automatically. No manual path is needed.

data.name: PresentMonStatusMissing
data.value: PresentMon was not found, so there is no frame data. It ships with the app; if it is missing, set its path under Settings.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackHint
data.value: When you mark stutter, the app keeps collecting for another 60 seconds before the finished incident appears in the list.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackSessionStarted
data.value: Session started. Waiting for PresentMon frames and the 30-second pre-buffer.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackCollectingFormat
data.value: {0} saved. The app understood the click and is collecting the rest of the capture window until {1}. Pending captures: {2}.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackReadyFormat
data.value: {0} is now ready. Select it in the incident list to inspect the analysis.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackReadyWithPendingFormat
data.value: {0} is now ready. There are still {1} capture(s) being collected.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackSyntheticReady
data.value: Synthetic incident created immediately for testing.

data.name: PacingIdle
data.value: No frame pacing data yet. The first window closes after a minute of frames.

data.name: PacingSaturatedFormat
data.value: {0} of {1} min ({2}), {3} marginal. Longest unbroken stretch {4} min.

data.name: PreLaunchHint
data.value: Ticked apps are asked to close, then FiveM starts. The choices are remembered.

data.name: PreLaunchNothingClosed
data.value: nothing, none of the ticked apps were running

data.name: CacheClearHint
data.value: Empties the folders FiveM downloads again by itself. Logins and in-game UI settings are left alone.

data.name: CacheClearConfirmFormat
data.value:
This deletes:
{0}
Freeing about {1}. The server downloads its resources again the next time you connect, so the first connection takes longer. Nothing else is touched.
Clear it?

data.name: CacheClearFailedFormat
data.value: {0} file(s) would not go, the first being {1}

data.name: CacheClearNothing
data.value: FiveM cache is already empty — nothing to clear.

data.name: CacheClearGameRunning
data.value: The cache cannot be cleared while FiveM is running. Close the game first.

data.name: SessionRetentionHint
data.value: Older journals, CSV files and deep captures are deleted at start. A session can leave several GB behind. 0 keeps everything.

data.name: SessionPrunedFormat
data.value: Housekeeping: {0} session file(s) older than {1} days deleted, {2} freed.

data.name: ServerProfileHint
data.value: Only used as a label in the incident list and exports.

data.name: NetworkHintsDescription
data.value: Use these only if you want extra network context in the incident timeline.

data.name: ProbeHostHint
data.value: Fill this in only if you know the game server host or IP and want ping samples. Otherwise leave it blank.

data.name: EndpointHintDescription
data.value: Optional readable host:port label for detected connections. Leave blank if you are unsure.

data.name: AdvancedSettingsDescription
data.value: Only open this if you need custom folders or want to override PresentMon/WPR paths.

data.name: AutoSessionEnabled
data.value: Start and stop the session with FiveM

data.name: AutoSessionStarted
data.value: FiveM was found — the session started by itself.

data.name: AutoSessionStoppedFormat
data.value: The game has been closed for {0:F0} minutes. The session is ending by itself and the summaries are written to the journal.

data.name: AutoSessionStartFailedFormat
data.value: The session could not be started automatically: {0}. Start it with the button.

data.name: AutoSessionStopFailedFormat
data.value: The session could not be ended automatically: {0}. Stop it with the button.

data.name: IncludeSensitiveFields
data.value: Include sensitive details (IP addresses, user name in paths)

data.name: LanguageChangeHint
data.value: Restart the app to apply language changes.

data.name: TrayReadyMessage
data.value: Right-click the tray icon to control diagnostics.

data.name: AppHiddenToTrayMessage
data.value: App hidden to tray. Diagnostics can keep running in the background.

data.name: TrayAutoSessionStopped
data.value: Session ended — everything is written to the journal.

data.name: HotkeyNoSessionMessage
data.value: Hotkey pressed, but no session is running — nothing was marked.

data.name: FakeDataDescription
data.value: Use this only when you want to validate the analysis engine without a live session.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackIncidentReady
data.value: PresentMon is delivering frames and the 30-second pre-buffer is complete. Ready for incident.

data.name: CaptureFeedbackWarmingFormat
data.value: Waiting for continuous PresentMon frames and pre-buffer: {0:F0}/{1:F0} seconds.

data.name: CaptureNormalManualIncidents
data.value: Deep capture for light marks too

data.name: SessionIdleAuto
data.value: Session idle. It starts by itself when FiveM appears.

data.name: SessionPostGameTail
data.value: The game closed. Measuring what the card releases.

data.name: SelectIncidentHint
data.value: Select an incident to inspect its summary and supporting evidence.

data.name: LiveVramPanelDescription
data.value: Live, refreshed with every sample. "Taken" is what a process has added since this session started — a program that took several hundred megabytes at once usually keeps them, and that is memory the game does not get.

data.name: LiveVramPanelEmpty
data.value: No process table yet. It appears once the session has found the FiveM/GTA process — VRAM is only measured while the game is running.

data.name: UpdateOnlyInReleaseBuilds
data.value: Updates can only be checked for in released builds.

data.name: UpdateUpToDate
data.value: You already have the latest version.

data.name: UpdateAvailableFormat
data.value:
FiveM Diagnostics {0} is available. You have {1}.
Download and install it now? The app closes and restarts automatically, and a running session is stopped.
Windows may ask for approval, or show a SmartScreen warning for a newly published or unsigned build.

data.name: UpdateCheckFailedFormat
data.value:
Could not check for or prepare the update.
{0}

data.name: UpdateInstallFailedFormat
data.value:
The update could not be completed, so the installed version was kept.
{0}

data.name: UpdateRollbackFormat
UpdateStatusWaitingForExit
data.value: Waiting for FiveM Diagnostics to close…

data.name: StartWithWindowsFailedFormat
data.value: Starting with Windows could not be changed: {0}

data.name: StartWithWindowsNotElevated
data.value: Start with Windows is on, but the app is not running as administrator right now. Windows will then start it without administrator rights, and deep capture will not work. Turn the option off and on again while the app runs as administrator.

data.name: NotElevatedBadge
data.value: Running without administrator rights: no deep capture.

data.name: SessionAutoHint
data.value: The session starts by itself when FiveM starts and ends ten minutes after the game closes. The buttons are for when you want to decide yourself.

data.name: ReadinessAdminOk
data.value: The app runs as administrator, so deep capture works.

data.name: ReadinessAdminMissing
data.value: Deep capture needs administrator rights. Without them the app still measures frames, CPU, memory, VRAM and network, but cannot record what the computer was doing during a stutter.

data.name: ReadinessStreamOn
data.value: You stream with OBS, so OBS and the stream are measured too. OBS's WebSocket server has to be enabled (Tools → WebSocket Server Settings).

data.name: ReadinessStreamOff
data.value: You don't stream, so OBS is not measured. Change it under Settings if you start.

data.name: ShareIntro
data.value: Pick an evening and create a zip with everything the app recorded: the journal with every incident, the measurement files and FiveM's own log. Explorer opens with the file selected, ready to drag into Discord or attach to a ticket.

data.name: ShareNoSessions
data.value: No recorded sessions yet. Play a session first.

data.name: ShareRedactHint
data.value: While unticked, IP addresses and your Windows user name in file paths are replaced with [redacted].

data.name: ShareIncludeTracesHint
data.value: Close to a gigabyte each and cannot be redacted. Only include them if the person helping you asks for them.

data.name: ShareUnreadableFormat
data.value: Locked by another program and left out: {0}.

data.name: ShareFailedFormat
data.value: The zip could not be created: {0}

data.name: StreamsHint
data.value: Off: OBS is not measured and nothing about streaming is shown. Takes effect at the next session.

data.name: HotkeysHint
data.value: Works while the game has focus. Write it like F9 or Ctrl+Shift+F9. The app takes the key for itself, so pick one the game and the server don't use.

data.name: HotkeyNoWindow
data.value: The hotkeys could not be attached to the window.

data.name: HotkeyUnparseableFormat
data.value: "{0}" is not a key the app understands. Change it under Settings.

data.name: HotkeyTakenFormat
data.value: Hotkey {0} could not be registered; another app holds it. Pick another under Settings.

data.name: LaunchArgumentsHint
data.value: Used by the launch button on Overview. Leave empty to start FiveM as usual.

data.name: SetupIntro
data.value: The app measures your computer while you play FiveM, so a stutter can be traced to its cause. Answer one question and check that everything can be measured.

data.name: SetupStreamQuestion
data.value: Do you stream with OBS while you play?

data.name: SetupStreamHint
data.value: Only changes what is measured and shown. You can change it later under Settings.

data.name: SetupHotkeysHint
data.value: Press it while you play when it stutters. It can be changed under Settings.

data.name: HotkeyLightHeader
data.value: Extra key: mark without a deep capture

data.name: HotkeyLightHint
data.value: Records the moment without saving a deep capture. Leave it empty to not use it.

data.name: HotkeyHintWithLightFormat
data.value: Hotkeys: {0} marks stutter, {1} makes a light mark without a deep capture.

data.name: PreLaunchEmpty
data.value: No programs yet. Add the ones that usually run while you play, or take one of the suggestions.

data.name: PreLaunchAddLabel
data.value: Add a program that is running
